## 1. Purpose

This module prepares the longitudinal *Coffea arabica* phenotypes used as
responses in the real-data genomic prediction workflow. The experiment contains
three annual evaluations, 13 experimental progenies, two checks, and an
augmented-block structure.

The module has four goals:

- **Describe the experiment:** make the years, progenies, checks, blocks,
  populations, plants, and traits explicit.
- **Fit the reference mixed model:** estimate fixed year means and the five
  random components used in the longitudinal phenotypic analysis.
- **Estimate variance components and BLUPs:** quantify progeny, permanent plant,
  population, block, progeny-by-year, and residual variation.
- **Prepare the genomic-prediction targets:** retain one BLUP for each of the 195
  target plants and each trait.

No marker data are used in this module. Genomic information enters only after
this phenotypic stage has been completed.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  cache = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "100%"
)

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

PHENOTYPE_INPUT <- "data/dados_reais/coffee_longitudinal_phenotypes.txt"
OUTPUT_DIR <- "output/real/phenotype"
FIGURE_DIR <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "figures")

dir.create(FIGURE_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## 2. Packages and fixed settings

### 2.1 Packages

Three packages support the reader-facing analysis:

- **`knitr`** formats experimental summaries and model results as HTML tables.
- **`ggplot2`** displays the annual phenotypic distributions.
- **`ggthemes`** applies the same visual style used in the simulated workflow.

The mixed model is fitted directly from its mixed-model equations. This makes
the variance-component estimation and stopping rule explicit in the tutorial.

```{r packages, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
```

### 2.2 Traits and fitting controls

The analyzed traits are `Cer`, `BM`, and `LP`. Zero is treated as a
non-observation during mixed-model fitting; this affects `LP` only.

```{r fitting-settings}
traits <- c("Cer", "BM", "LP")

tolerance <- c(
  Cer = 0.05,
  BM = 0.05,
  LP = 0.0001
)

fitting_settings <- data.frame(
  Trait = traits,
  Tolerance = unname(tolerance[traits]),
  Zero_treated_as_non_observation = TRUE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

fitting_settings |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Trait-specific fitting settings",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%; max-width:100%;"'
  )
```

## 3. Experimental data

### 3.1 Canonical variables

The phenotype file uses descriptive names so the experimental structure can be
read directly from the analysis.

```{r read-phenotypes}
phenotype <- read.delim(
  PHENOTYPE_INPUT,
  header = TRUE,
  sep = "\t",
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

expected_columns <- c(
  "Observacao", "Progenie", "Ano", "ID_Planta", "Populacao",
  "Bloco", "Progenie_Ano", "Planta", "Cer", "BM", "LP"
)

stopifnot(
  identical(names(phenotype), expected_columns),
  nrow(phenotype) == 684L,
  ncol(phenotype) == 11L,
  !anyNA(phenotype)
)

variable_dictionary <- data.frame(
  Variable = expected_columns,
  Interpretation = c(
    "Observation index",
    "Progeny; 1-13 experimental and 14-15 checks",
    "Evaluation year",
    "Permanent individual plant identifier",
    "Population",
    "Block",
    "Progeny-by-year identifier",
    "Plant number within progeny",
    "Cercosporiosis score",
    "Vegetative vigor score",
    "Yield-related longitudinal measurement"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

variable_dictionary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Variables in the longitudinal phenotype file",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%; max-width:100%;"'
  )
```

### 3.2 Longitudinal and augmented-block structure

The 684 records correspond to 228 permanent plant identifiers evaluated in
2014, 2015, and 2016. Progenies 1-13 form the genomic-prediction population.
Progenies 14 and 15 are checks in the augmented-block experiment and remain in
the phenotypic mixed-model fit.

```{r experimental-structure}
target <- phenotype[phenotype$Progenie %in% 1:13, , drop = FALSE]
checks <- phenotype[phenotype$Progenie %in% 14:15, , drop = FALSE]

structure_summary <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c(
    "Longitudinal observations", "Evaluation years", "Progenies",
    "Experimental progenies", "Check progenies", "Permanent plant identifiers",
    "Target plants", "Check plant identifiers", "Blocks", "Populations",
    "Progeny-by-year levels"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(phenotype), length(unique(phenotype$Ano)),
    length(unique(phenotype$Progenie)), length(unique(target$Progenie)),
    length(unique(checks$Progenie)), length(unique(phenotype$ID_Planta)),
    length(unique(target$ID_Planta)), length(unique(checks$ID_Planta)),
    length(unique(phenotype$Bloco)), length(unique(phenotype$Populacao)),
    length(unique(phenotype$Progenie_Ano))
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

structure_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Experimental structure of the longitudinal coffee data",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%; max-width:100%;"'
  )

target_repetitions <- table(table(target$ID_Planta))
target_year_table <- table(
  target$ID_Planta,
  target$Ano
)
target_years <- rowSums(
  target_year_table > 0
)

stopifnot(
  identical(sort(unique(phenotype$Ano)), c(2014L, 2015L, 2016L)),
  length(unique(phenotype$Progenie)) == 15L,
  length(unique(phenotype$ID_Planta)) == 228L,
  length(unique(target$ID_Planta)) == 195L,
  length(unique(checks$ID_Planta)) == 33L,
  length(intersect(unique(target$ID_Planta), unique(checks$ID_Planta))) == 0L,
  length(target_repetitions) == 1L,
  as.integer(target_repetitions) == 195L,
  as.integer(names(target_repetitions)) == 3L,
  all(target_years == 3L)
)
```

For the experimental progenies,

\[
13\ \text{progenies}\times15\ \text{plants}=195\ \text{target plants}.
\]

`ID_Planta` therefore identifies the same individual plant across all three
evaluation years.

## 4. Phenotypic traits

### 4.1 Descriptive summaries

The raw observations are summarized before model fitting. These summaries show
the original scale and annual variation; they do not replace the mixed-model
adjustment.

```{r trait-summary}
trait_summary <- data.frame()

for (trait in traits) {

  x <- phenotype[[trait]]

  trait_summary <- rbind(
    trait_summary,
    data.frame(
      Trait = trait,
      N = sum(is.finite(x)),
      Mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      SD = stats::sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Minimum = min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Maximum = max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Zero_count = sum(x == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  )
}

rownames(trait_summary) <- NULL

trait_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Raw phenotypic summaries",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%; max-width:100%;"'
  )

year_summary <- data.frame()

for (trait in traits) {

  for (year in sort(unique(phenotype$Ano))) {

    x <- phenotype[
      phenotype$Ano == year,
      trait
    ]

    year_summary <- rbind(
      year_summary,
      data.frame(
        Trait = trait,
        Year = year,
        N = length(x),
        Mean = mean(x),
        SD = stats::sd(x),
        Minimum = min(x),
        Maximum = max(x),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    )
  }
}

rownames(year_summary) <- NULL

year_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Phenotypic summaries by evaluation year",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%; max-width:100%;"'
  )
```

### 4.2 Annual distributions

The observations are separated by evaluation year to show the temporal
variation present before mixed-model adjustment. This view helps explain why
year is represented explicitly in the model instead of averaging the annual
measurements before analysis.

```{r phenotype-distributions, fig.cap="Annual phenotypic distributions for the three coffee traits."}
phenotype_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(Year = phenotype$Ano, Trait = "Cer", Value = phenotype$Cer),
  data.frame(Year = phenotype$Ano, Trait = "BM", Value = phenotype$BM),
  data.frame(Year = phenotype$Ano, Trait = "LP", Value = phenotype$LP)
)

phenotype_long$Year <- factor(
  phenotype_long$Year,
  levels = c(2014, 2015, 2016)
)

p_traits <- ggplot(
  phenotype_long,
  aes(x = Year, y = Value, fill = Year)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.65,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Trait,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  scale_fill_gdocs() +
  labs(
    x = "Evaluation year",
    y = "Observed phenotype"
  ) +
  theme_gdocs()

print(p_traits)
```

```{r save-phenotype-distributions, include=FALSE}
ggsave(
  file.path(
    FIGURE_DIR,
    "annual_phenotypic_distributions.tiff"
  ),
  plot = p_traits,
  device = "tiff",
  width = 9,
  height = 5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300,
  compression = "lzw"
)
```

## 5. Longitudinal mixed model

### 5.1 Statistical formulation

Each trait is analyzed separately with

\[
\mathbf{y}
=
\mathbf{X}\mathbf{u}
+
\mathbf{Z}\mathbf{g}
+
\mathbf{W}\mathbf{p}
+
\mathbf{V}\mathbf{r}
+
\mathbf{T}\mathbf{b}
+
\mathbf{R}\mathbf{i}
+
\mathbf{e},
\]

where:

- \(\mathbf{u}\): fixed evaluation-year means;
- \(\mathbf{g}\): random progeny effects;
- \(\mathbf{p}\): random permanent individual plant effects;
- \(\mathbf{r}\): random population effects;
- \(\mathbf{b}\): random block effects;
- \(\mathbf{i}\): random progeny-by-year interaction effects;
- \(\mathbf{e}\): residual variation.

The model separates permanent differences among plants from annual and
experimental sources of variation.

```{r model-terms}
model_terms <- data.frame(
  Model_component = c(
    "Fixed year", "Progeny", "Permanent individual plant", "Population",
    "Block", "Progeny x year", "Residual"
  ),
  Data_field = c(
    "Ano", "Progenie", "ID_Planta", "Populacao", "Bloco", "Progenie_Ano", "-"
  ),
  Type = c("Fixed", rep("Random", 5), "Residual"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

model_terms |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Terms in the longitudinal phenotypic mixed model",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%; max-width:100%;"'
  )
```

`Planta` is retained for identification but is not fitted as an additional
random effect because `ID_Planta` already represents the permanent individual
plant.

## 6. Mixed-model equations

### 6.1 Preparing each trait

Zero is treated as a non-observation during mixed-model fitting. `Cer` and
`BM` therefore retain all 684 records, whereas seven zero `LP` records are
excluded.

The three analysis data sets are created explicitly so the reader can see
which observations enter each model.

```{r prepare-traits}
cer_data <- phenotype
cer_data$y <- as.numeric(cer_data$Cer)
cer_data <- cer_data[
  is.finite(cer_data$y) & cer_data$y != 0,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

bm_data <- phenotype
bm_data$y <- as.numeric(bm_data$BM)
bm_data <- bm_data[
  is.finite(bm_data$y) & bm_data$y != 0,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

lp_data <- phenotype
lp_data$y <- as.numeric(lp_data$LP)
lp_data <- lp_data[
  is.finite(lp_data$y) & lp_data$y != 0,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

analysis_data <- list(
  Cer = cer_data,
  BM = bm_data,
  LP = lp_data
)

records_used <- data.frame(
  Trait = c("Cer", "BM", "LP"),
  Records_available = rep(nrow(phenotype), 3),
  Records_used = c(
    nrow(cer_data),
    nrow(bm_data),
    nrow(lp_data)
  ),
  Records_excluded = c(
    nrow(phenotype) - nrow(cer_data),
    nrow(phenotype) - nrow(bm_data),
    nrow(phenotype) - nrow(lp_data)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

records_used |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Records entering each trait-specific mixed model",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%; max-width:100%;"'
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(cer_data) == 684L,
  nrow(bm_data) == 684L,
  nrow(lp_data) == 677L
)
```

### 6.2 Incidence matrices

For each trait, the fixed-effect matrix contains one indicator column for each
year. Five additional incidence matrices represent progeny, permanent plant,
population, block, and progeny-by-year interaction.

The matrices are created directly inside the fitting loop with `model.matrix()`.
The factor levels follow their first appearance in the data so the mixed-model
equations retain the same ordering throughout the analysis.

## 7. REML variance-component estimation

The fitting procedure starts from variance proportions of 0.10 for each random
effect and 0.50 for the residual. Thus the initial variance ratio for every
random component is

\[
\lambda_j=\frac{0.50}{0.10}=5.
\]

At each iteration, the mixed-model equations are solved and the residual
variance is updated by

\[
\widehat{\sigma}_e^2
=
\frac{
\mathbf{e}'\mathbf{e}
+
\sum_j \lambda_j\mathbf{u}_j'\mathbf{u}_j
}{
n-\operatorname{rank}(\mathbf{X})
},
\]

while each random-effect variance is updated by

\[
\widehat{\sigma}_j^2
=
\frac{
\mathbf{u}_j'\mathbf{u}_j
+
\widehat{\sigma}_e^2\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{C}_{jj})
}{q_j}.
\]

The loop stops when the largest absolute change among the five random variance
proportions is smaller than or equal to the trait-specific tolerance.

```{r fit-models}
fits <- list()

for (trait in traits) {

  d <- analysis_data[[trait]]

  year_levels <- unique(d$Ano)
  progeny_levels <- unique(d$Progenie)
  plant_levels <- unique(d$ID_Planta)
  population_levels <- unique(d$Populacao)
  block_levels <- unique(d$Bloco)
  progeny_year_levels <- unique(d$Progenie_Ano)

  X <- model.matrix(
    ~ 0 + factor(Ano, levels = year_levels),
    data = d
  )

  Z_progeny <- model.matrix(
    ~ 0 + factor(Progenie, levels = progeny_levels),
    data = d
  )

  Z_plant <- model.matrix(
    ~ 0 + factor(ID_Planta, levels = plant_levels),
    data = d
  )

  Z_population <- model.matrix(
    ~ 0 + factor(Populacao, levels = population_levels),
    data = d
  )

  Z_block <- model.matrix(
    ~ 0 + factor(Bloco, levels = block_levels),
    data = d
  )

  Z_progeny_year <- model.matrix(
    ~ 0 + factor(Progenie_Ano, levels = progeny_year_levels),
    data = d
  )

  W <- cbind(
    X,
    Z_progeny,
    Z_plant,
    Z_population,
    Z_block,
    Z_progeny_year
  )

  p <- ncol(X)

  start_progeny <- p + 1L
  end_progeny <- start_progeny + ncol(Z_progeny) - 1L

  start_plant <- end_progeny + 1L
  end_plant <- start_plant + ncol(Z_plant) - 1L

  start_population <- end_plant + 1L
  end_population <- start_population + ncol(Z_population) - 1L

  start_block <- end_population + 1L
  end_block <- start_block + ncol(Z_block) - 1L

  start_progeny_year <- end_block + 1L
  end_progeny_year <- start_progeny_year + ncol(Z_progeny_year) - 1L

  idx_progeny <- start_progeny:end_progeny
  idx_plant <- start_plant:end_plant
  idx_population <- start_population:end_population
  idx_block <- start_block:end_block
  idx_progeny_year <- start_progeny_year:end_progeny_year

  old_props <- c(
    Progenie = 0.10,
    ID_Planta = 0.10,
    Populacao = 0.10,
    Bloco = 0.10,
    Progenie_Ano = 0.10,
    Residual = 0.50
  )

  history <- data.frame(
    Trait = character(),
    Iteration = integer(),
    Maximum_change = numeric(),
    Tolerance = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  for (iteration in seq_len(500L)) {

    lambda_progeny <- old_props["Residual"] / old_props["Progenie"]
    lambda_plant <- old_props["Residual"] / old_props["ID_Planta"]
    lambda_population <- old_props["Residual"] / old_props["Populacao"]
    lambda_block <- old_props["Residual"] / old_props["Bloco"]
    lambda_progeny_year <- old_props["Residual"] / old_props["Progenie_Ano"]

    penalty <- matrix(
      0,
      nrow = ncol(W),
      ncol = ncol(W)
    )

    penalty[idx_progeny, idx_progeny] <- diag(
      as.numeric(lambda_progeny),
      length(idx_progeny)
    )

    penalty[idx_plant, idx_plant] <- diag(
      as.numeric(lambda_plant),
      length(idx_plant)
    )

    penalty[idx_population, idx_population] <- diag(
      as.numeric(lambda_population),
      length(idx_population)
    )

    penalty[idx_block, idx_block] <- diag(
      as.numeric(lambda_block),
      length(idx_block)
    )

    penalty[idx_progeny_year, idx_progeny_year] <- diag(
      as.numeric(lambda_progeny_year),
      length(idx_progeny_year)
    )

    M <- crossprod(W) + penalty
    rhs <- crossprod(W, d$y)

    coefficients <- solve(M, rhs)
    C <- solve(M)

    fitted_values <- as.numeric(W %*% coefficients)
    residuals <- d$y - fitted_values

    u_progeny <- coefficients[idx_progeny]
    u_plant <- coefficients[idx_plant]
    u_population <- coefficients[idx_population]
    u_block <- coefficients[idx_block]
    u_progeny_year <- coefficients[idx_progeny_year]

    penalized_ss <- (
      sum(residuals^2) +
      as.numeric(lambda_progeny) * sum(u_progeny^2) +
      as.numeric(lambda_plant) * sum(u_plant^2) +
      as.numeric(lambda_population) * sum(u_population^2) +
      as.numeric(lambda_block) * sum(u_block^2) +
      as.numeric(lambda_progeny_year) * sum(u_progeny_year^2)
    )

    df_reml <- nrow(d) - ncol(X)
    residual_variance <- penalized_ss / df_reml

    V_progeny <- (
      sum(u_progeny^2) +
      residual_variance *
        sum(diag(C[idx_progeny, idx_progeny, drop = FALSE]))
    ) / length(idx_progeny)

    V_plant <- (
      sum(u_plant^2) +
      residual_variance *
        sum(diag(C[idx_plant, idx_plant, drop = FALSE]))
    ) / length(idx_plant)

    V_population <- (
      sum(u_population^2) +
      residual_variance *
        sum(diag(C[idx_population, idx_population, drop = FALSE]))
    ) / length(idx_population)

    V_block <- (
      sum(u_block^2) +
      residual_variance *
        sum(diag(C[idx_block, idx_block, drop = FALSE]))
    ) / length(idx_block)

    V_progeny_year <- (
      sum(u_progeny_year^2) +
      residual_variance *
        sum(diag(C[
          idx_progeny_year,
          idx_progeny_year,
          drop = FALSE
        ]))
    ) / length(idx_progeny_year)

    components <- c(
      Progenie = V_progeny,
      ID_Planta = V_plant,
      Populacao = V_population,
      Bloco = V_block,
      Progenie_Ano = V_progeny_year,
      Residual = residual_variance
    )

    phenotypic_variance <- sum(components)
    new_props <- components / phenotypic_variance

    lambda_new <- residual_variance / components[
      c(
        "Progenie",
        "ID_Planta",
        "Populacao",
        "Bloco",
        "Progenie_Ano"
      )
    ]

    logdet_M <- as.numeric(
      determinant(
        M,
        logarithm = TRUE
      )$modulus
    )

    deviance <- (
      df_reml * (1 + log(residual_variance)) +
      logdet_M -
      (
        length(idx_progeny) * log(lambda_new["Progenie"]) +
        length(idx_plant) * log(lambda_new["ID_Planta"]) +
        length(idx_population) * log(lambda_new["Populacao"]) +
        length(idx_block) * log(lambda_new["Bloco"]) +
        length(idx_progeny_year) * log(lambda_new["Progenie_Ano"])
      )
    )

    random_change <- max(
      abs(
        new_props[
          c(
            "Progenie",
            "ID_Planta",
            "Populacao",
            "Bloco",
            "Progenie_Ano"
          )
        ] -
        old_props[
          c(
            "Progenie",
            "ID_Planta",
            "Populacao",
            "Bloco",
            "Progenie_Ano"
          )
        ]
      )
    )

    history <- rbind(
      history,
      data.frame(
        Trait = trait,
        Iteration = iteration,
        Maximum_change = random_change,
        Tolerance = tolerance[[trait]],
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    )

    if (random_change <= tolerance[[trait]]) {
      break
    }

    old_props <- new_props
  }

  if (random_change > tolerance[[trait]]) {
    stop(
      trait,
      ": stopping rule not reached within 500 iterations."
    )
  }

  beta <- coefficients[seq_len(p)]
  names(beta) <- as.character(year_levels)

  names(u_progeny) <- as.character(progeny_levels)
  names(u_plant) <- as.character(plant_levels)
  names(u_population) <- as.character(population_levels)
  names(u_block) <- as.character(block_levels)
  names(u_progeny_year) <- as.character(progeny_year_levels)

  fits[[trait]] <- list(
    trait = trait,
    data = d,
    final = list(
      components = components,
      proportions = new_props,
      beta = beta,
      u = list(
        Progenie = u_progeny,
        ID_Planta = u_plant,
        Populacao = u_population,
        Bloco = u_block,
        Progenie_Ano = u_progeny_year
      ),
      residual = residuals,
      fitted = fitted_values,
      C = C,
      deviance = as.numeric(deviance),
      random_change = random_change
    ),
    history = history,
    iterations = iteration,
    tolerance = tolerance[[trait]]
  )
}
```

The code above exposes the complete path from the incidence matrices to the
variance updates and BLUP solutions without hiding any step in project-specific
helper functions.

## 8. Variance components and genetic parameters

For each trait,

\[
V_f=V_g+V_p+V_r+V_b+V_i+V_e.
\]

The variance proportions, repeatability, and total heritability are calculated
directly from the fitted components.

```{r variance-components}
variance_components <- data.frame()

for (trait in traits) {

  fit <- fits[[trait]]
  components <- fit$final$components
  props <- fit$final$proportions
  Vf <- sum(components)

  variance_components <- rbind(
    variance_components,
    data.frame(
      Trait = trait,
      N = nrow(fit$data),
      Iterations = fit$iterations,
      Tolerance = fit$tolerance,
      Deviance = fit$final$deviance,
      V_progeny = components["Progenie"],
      V_plant = components["ID_Planta"],
      V_population = components["Populacao"],
      V_block = components["Bloco"],
      V_progeny_year = components["Progenie_Ano"],
      V_residual = components["Residual"],
      V_phenotypic = Vf,
      h2_progeny = props["Progenie"],
      c2_plant = props["ID_Planta"],
      h2_population = props["Populacao"],
      c2_block = props["Bloco"],
      c2_progeny_year = props["Progenie_Ano"],
      Repeatability = (
        components["Progenie"] +
        components["ID_Planta"] +
        components["Populacao"] +
        components["Bloco"]
      ) / Vf,
      h2_total = (
        components["Progenie"] +
        components["Populacao"]
      ) / Vf,
      Overall_mean = mean(fit$final$beta),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  )
}

rownames(variance_components) <- NULL

variance_table <- variance_components[
  ,
  c(
    "Trait",
    "N",
    "Iterations",
    "V_progeny",
    "V_plant",
    "V_population",
    "V_block",
    "V_progeny_year",
    "V_residual",
    "V_phenotypic"
  )
]

variance_table |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 6,
    caption = "Variance components from the longitudinal mixed model",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%; max-width:100%;"'
  )

parameter_table <- variance_components[
  ,
  c(
    "Trait",
    "h2_progeny",
    "c2_plant",
    "h2_population",
    "c2_block",
    "c2_progeny_year",
    "Repeatability",
    "h2_total",
    "Overall_mean"
  )
]

parameter_table |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 6,
    caption = "Variance ratios and genetic parameters",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%; max-width:100%;"'
  )
```

Separating the variance components from the derived parameters keeps both
tables readable at the width of the tutorial page.

## 9. Fixed year effects

The fixed solutions estimate the adjusted mean for each evaluation year after
the random experimental and biological effects have been accounted for.

```{r fixed-year-effects}
fixed_year_effects <- data.frame()

for (trait in traits) {

  fit <- fits[[trait]]

  fixed_year_effects <- rbind(
    fixed_year_effects,
    data.frame(
      Trait = trait,
      Year = as.integer(
        names(fit$final$beta)
      ),
      Adjusted_mean = as.numeric(
        fit$final$beta
      ),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  )
}

rownames(fixed_year_effects) <- NULL

fixed_year_effects |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Adjusted fixed means by evaluation year",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%; max-width:100%;"'
  )
```

## 10. BLUPs for the 195 target plants

### 10.1 Individual identity

For progenies 1-13, `ID_Planta` is in one-to-one correspondence with progeny
and plant number and is repeated over the three years.

```{r target-identity}
target_map <- unique(
  target[, c("ID_Planta", "Progenie", "Planta", "Populacao")]
)

target_map <- target_map[
  order(target_map$Progenie, target_map$Planta),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
rownames(target_map) <- NULL

stopifnot(
  nrow(target_map) == 195L,
  length(unique(target_map$ID_Planta)) == 195L
)

target_map$Phenotype_ID <- sprintf(
  "PROG%02d_PL%02d",
  target_map$Progenie,
  target_map$Planta
)

head(target_map, 15) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "First 15 target plants used for genomic prediction",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%; max-width:100%;"'
  )
```

### 10.2 One BLUP per plant

For genomic prediction, one BLUP is retained for each target plant and trait.
The year, block, and progeny-by-year terms describe evaluation-specific or
experimental variation and are not carried forward as permanent plant values.

For plant \(k\), the BLUP is calculated as

\[
\widehat{y}_k =
\widehat{\mu}
+
\widehat{g}_{j(k)}
+
\widehat{p}_k
+
\widehat{r}_{m(k)},
\]

where \(\widehat{\mu}\) is the overall adjusted mean,
\(\widehat{g}_{j(k)}\) is the progeny effect,
\(\widehat{p}_k\) is the permanent individual-plant effect, and
\(\widehat{r}_{m(k)}\) is the population effect.

The code keeps these components explicit so the construction of each BLUP can
be followed directly.

```{r individual-blups}
blup_tables <- list()

for (trait in traits) {

  fit <- fits[[trait]]
  u <- fit$final$u
  overall_mean <- mean(fit$final$beta)

  out <- target_map

  out$Progeny_effect <- as.numeric(
    u$Progenie[
      as.character(out$Progenie)
    ]
  )

  out$Plant_effect <- as.numeric(
    u$ID_Planta[
      as.character(out$ID_Planta)
    ]
  )

  out$Population_effect <- as.numeric(
    u$Populacao[
      as.character(out$Populacao)
    ]
  )

  stopifnot(
    !anyNA(out$Progeny_effect),
    !anyNA(out$Plant_effect),
    !anyNA(out$Population_effect)
  )

  out$BLUP <- (
    overall_mean +
    out$Progeny_effect +
    out$Plant_effect +
    out$Population_effect
  )

  blup_tables[[trait]] <- out
}
```

For `Cer`, the first plants can be inspected together with the three fitted
components that form their BLUP.

```{r blup-components-example}
head(
  blup_tables$Cer[
    ,
    c(
      "Phenotype_ID",
      "Progenie",
      "Planta",
      "Progeny_effect",
      "Plant_effect",
      "Population_effect",
      "BLUP"
    )
  ],
  15
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Components of the first 15 Cer BLUPs",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%; max-width:100%;"'
  )
```

The three trait-specific BLUP vectors are then placed in a single table with
one row for each of the 195 target plants.

```{r combine-individual-blups}
blups <- target_map[
  ,
  c(
    "Phenotype_ID",
    "ID_Planta",
    "Progenie",
    "Planta",
    "Populacao"
  )
]

blups$Cer <- blup_tables$Cer$BLUP
blups$BM <- blup_tables$BM$BLUP
blups$LP <- blup_tables$LP$BLUP

blups <- blups[
  order(
    blups$Progenie,
    blups$Planta
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

rownames(blups) <- NULL

stopifnot(
  nrow(blups) == 195L,
  !anyNA(blups[, traits]),
  length(unique(blups$Phenotype_ID)) == 195L
)

head(blups, 15) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "First 15 BLUPs prepared for genomic prediction",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%; max-width:100%;"'
  )
```

### 10.3 BLUP distributions

The distributions of the 195 BLUPs can now be examined on the same three trait
scales used for the raw phenotypes. This makes the effect of the mixed-model
adjustment visible before the values enter the genomic-prediction workflow.

```{r blup-distributions, fig.cap="Distribution of the BLUPs for the 195 target coffee plants."}
blup_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(Trait = "Cer", BLUP = blups$Cer),
  data.frame(Trait = "BM", BLUP = blups$BM),
  data.frame(Trait = "LP", BLUP = blups$LP)
)

p_blup_distribution <- ggplot(
  blup_long,
  aes(
    x = BLUP,
    fill = Trait,
    colour = Trait
  )
) +
  geom_density(
    alpha = 0.28,
    linewidth = 0.9,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Trait,
    scales = "free"
  ) +
  scale_fill_gdocs() +
  scale_color_gdocs() +
  labs(
    x = "BLUP",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_gdocs()

print(p_blup_distribution)
```

```{r save-blup-distributions, include=FALSE}
ggsave(
  file.path(
    FIGURE_DIR,
    "blup_distributions.tiff"
  ),
  plot = p_blup_distribution,
  device = "tiff",
  width = 9,
  height = 5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300,
  compression = "lzw"
)
```

These 195 rows are the phenotypic targets passed to the next real-data module.
Marker information has not been used to estimate or select any of these values.

## 11. Numerical reproducibility check

The implementation includes an internal numerical regression test to detect
unintended changes in the mixed-model calculations. The values below are used
only for this test and do not participate in fitting.

```{r regression-benchmark, include=FALSE}
benchmark <- data.frame(
  Trait = c("Cer", "BM", "LP"),
  N = c(684L, 684L, 677L),
  Iterations = c(1L, 1L, 46L),
  V_progeny = c(0.046499, 0.031433, 0.751094),
  V_plant = c(0.068135, 0.049095, 1.886503),
  V_population = c(0.050455, 0.027236, 0.039846),
  V_block = c(0.036630, 0.032487, 0.234072),
  V_progeny_year = c(0.057987, 0.031809, 0.067444),
  V_residual = c(0.384139, 0.258941, 5.055057),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

component_columns <- c(
  "V_progeny", "V_plant", "V_population", "V_block", "V_progeny_year", "V_residual"
)

for (trait in traits) {
  observed <- variance_components[variance_components$Trait == trait, , drop = FALSE]
  expected <- benchmark[benchmark$Trait == trait, , drop = FALSE]

  stopifnot(
    observed$N == expected$N,
    observed$Iterations == expected$Iterations,
    max(abs(
      as.numeric(observed[1, component_columns]) -
      as.numeric(expected[1, component_columns])
    )) < 5e-6
  )
}
```

## 12. Canonical outputs

The module saves the 195 individual BLUPs, variance components, complete model
effects, descriptive summaries, and run metadata.

```{r save-outputs}
utils::write.csv(
  blups,
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "real_phenotype_blups.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

saveRDS(
  blups,
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "real_phenotype_blups.rds")
)

utils::write.csv(
  variance_components,
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "real_phenotype_variance_components.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

saveRDS(
  variance_components,
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "real_phenotype_variance_components.rds")
)

model_effects <- list()

for (trait in traits) {
  model_effects[[trait]] <- list(
    fixed_year = fits[[trait]]$final$beta,
    random = fits[[trait]]$final$u
  )
}

saveRDS(
  model_effects,
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "real_phenotype_model_effects.rds")
)

utils::write.csv(
  trait_summary,
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "real_phenotype_summary.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

run_metadata <- list(
  generated_at = Sys.time(),
  R_version = R.version.string,
  input = PHENOTYPE_INPUT,
  observations = nrow(phenotype),
  years = sort(unique(phenotype$Ano)),
  progenies = sort(unique(phenotype$Progenie)),
  checks = c(14L, 15L),
  target_plants = nrow(blups),
  traits = traits,
  tolerances = tolerance,
  model = paste(
    "fixed Ano; random Progenie + ID_Planta +",
    "Populacao + Bloco + Progenie_Ano"
  )
)

saveRDS(
  run_metadata,
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "real_phenotype_run_metadata.rds")
)
```

The central product is `real_phenotype_blups.rds`, containing exactly 195 target
plants and the three trait BLUPs. Genotype matching and marker quality control
are performed only in the next stage.

## 13. Reproducibility conclusion

The longitudinal phenotype stage has a single explicit contract:

- the canonical input contains 684 observations from 2014-2016;
- the two checks remain in the mixed-model fit;
- year is fixed;
- progeny, permanent individual plant, population, block, and progeny-by-year
  interaction are random;
- zero values are excluded from mixed-model fitting;
- the normalized data reproduce the established variance components;
- 195 target plants receive one BLUP for each trait;
- no genomic information is used before phenotypic adjustment is complete.

The resulting BLUP table is the phenotypic input to the real-data genomic
workflow.
